procedure: The root and independent source-only reviewers inspected all eleven primary-source renderings. The preserved reconciliation accepted the independent coverage findings and added the three distinct objects. This snapshot binds the resulting exact inventory content; it does not judge any Lean target.

rows.source_label: Physical conservation of pressure and velocity is only approximate for very small disturbances in uniform media

disposition.reason: This is the empirical small-disturbance modeling qualification. The separate ACOUSTICS-CONSERVATION-FORM row covers the exact algebraic assertion from the same paragraph.

rows.source_label: The constant-coefficient linear acoustics equations have conservation form for pressure and velocity
The acoustics matrix in (1.6) has eigenvalues -c and +c
w2 = p - rho c u satisfies w2_t - c w2_x = 0 and the printed left-going profile is q2(x,t) = qtilde(x+ct)
For c = sqrt(K/rho), w1 = p + rho c u satisfies w1_t + c w1_x = 0
The two-equation acoustics system decomposes into two scalar waves moving in opposite directions
Contaminant mass conservation with flux f(q) = ubar q yields the advection equation
Equations (1.2) and (1.4) are mathematically identical after renaming the unknown and speed
On rectangular or logically rectangular grids, dimensional splitting solves one-dimensional coordinate-direction problems in turn
At a discontinuity the differential equation fails classically while the integral conservation law continues to hold
Every vector in R^m decomposes uniquely as a linear combination of the eigenvectors
The eigenvalues of A give the speeds of the component waves
Equation (1.1): q_t + A q_x = 0 for a constant real m by m matrix A
Equation (1.10): for any two points x1 and x2, the time derivative of the interval integral is f(q(x1,t)) minus f(q(x2,t))
Equation (1.11): Riemann initial data is q_l for x below zero and q_r for x above zero
Equation (1.2): q_t + ubar q_x = 0 for constant advection speed ubar
Equation (1.3): q(x,t) = qtilde(x - ubar t) solves the advection equation and propagates unchanged
Equation (1.4): w_t + c w_x = 0 with c positive models a right-going one-way wave
Equation (1.5): p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0
Equation (1.6): q = (p,u) and A = [[0,K],[1/rho,0]]
Equation (1.7): differentiating (1.5) and eliminating mixed derivatives gives p_tt = c^2 p_xx
Equation (1.8): q_t + f(q)_x = 0 with flux function f
Equation (1.9): q_t + f'(q) q_x = 0 is the quasilinear form
A finite-volume unknown is the cell integral divided by cell volume rather than a point value
A time step modifies cell averages by edge fluxes computed from the available approximate averages
The quasilinear form suggests hyperbolicity when the flux Jacobian satisfies the matrix condition
Assign heterogeneous material properties to each cell by averaging parameters over its volume
A constant-coefficient system is hyperbolic when A has real eigenvalues and m linearly independent eigenvectors
Every constant real hyperbolic system decouples in an eigenbasis into scalar advection equations, with reconstruction of the state
Sufficient smoothness of q and f(q) permits deriving (1.8) from the integral law (1.10)
Equation (1.1) is a conservation law with linear flux f(q) = A q
Solve linear hyperbolic Riemann data using eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A
Material-interface Riemann dynamics decomposes reflected and transmitted waves into neighboring cells

disposition.reason: The reflected/transmitted-wave assertion omits the governing heterogeneous equations, interface conditions, wave families, and solver. The precise joint material/state initial-data construction is retained separately as MATERIAL-INTERFACE-RIEMANN-DATA; no wave-dynamics guarantee is inferred from that data definition.

rows.source_label: Material-interface Riemann initial data prescribes jumps in both medium and state at x=0
Use a normal Riemann solve at each two-dimensional edge or approximately planar three-dimensional face to determine flux

disposition.reason: The chapter gives an implementation pattern without fixing a multidimensional mesh model, face orientation, normal-flux function, approximate Riemann solver, or update formula.

rows.source_label: If contaminant mass is not conserved, the conservation law must contain source terms
The simple wave structure extends to nonlinear systems with exact or arbitrarily accurate Riemann solutions constructible even for Euler

disposition.reason: The broad exact-or-arbitrarily-accurate nonlinear construction claim fixes no system/domain, solver, error metric, admissibility class, existence hypotheses, or accuracy parameter. These missing truth conditions, rather than the later-chapter reference or a missing implementation, prevent a unique contract here.

rows.source_label: Nonlinear conservation laws can develop discontinuities spontaneously from smooth initial data
Superscripts enumerate eigenvalues lambda^p and eigenvectors r^p

disposition.reason: Editorial superscript convention for a finite eigenfamily; the mathematical eigenbasis content is separately inventoried.

rows.source_label: Initial data is denoted by a circle over the variable

disposition.reason: The circle accent is purely a printed convention for initial data and contributes no proposition or reusable mathematical definition.

rows.source_label: Q_i^n and Q_ij^n denote numerical approximations; subscripts are spatial and n is the time level

disposition.reason: Editorial subscript/superscript convention for cell and time indices. Mathematical arrays, averaging and current-step dependence have separate inventory coverage.

rows.source_label: psi and p are deliberately overloaded in separated contexts

disposition.reason: The passage is an editorial warning about context-dependent printed symbols, not a claim suitable for a Lean declaration.

rows.source_label: q denotes the PDE solution while u is reserved for velocity or the x component of (u,v)

disposition.reason: Editorial choice of names for the solution and physical velocity; the equation roles are inventoried separately.

rows.source_label: For m equations q and Q are m-vectors and q^p denotes component p

disposition.reason: Editorial notation for components of the m-dimensional state and numerical array. Dimension and field shape are covered by the system and finite-volume definitions.

rows.source_label: In a one-step method the solution at the next time level is determined entirely by data at the current time level
Riemann initial-value configuration: a hyperbolic equation together with piecewise constant two-state initial data
Use neighboring cell averages as Riemann states to obtain numerical-flux and update information
The q-Riemann symbol denotes the similarity-solution value along x/t = 0 for data q_l and q_r
A hyperbolic Riemann solution is typically a function of x/t with finitely many constant-speed waves

disposition.reason: The source explicitly qualifies this as typical and gives no theorem hypotheses, wave-count bound, admissibility condition, or nonlinear solution class.

rows.source_label: The real scalar constant-coefficient equation is hyperbolic
Equation (1.7) is hyperbolic under the standard classification of second-order linear equations
Shock capturing avoids explicit tracking, smears jumps over cells, and seeks correct jump conditions without nonphysical oscillations

disposition.reason: The source describes a desired method class and qualitative behavior but specifies neither a numerical update nor definitions of smearing, correct jump conditions, or nonphysical oscillation.

rows.source_label: Shock or front tracking combines a smooth-region scheme with explicit discontinuity tracking and jump conditions

disposition.reason: The paragraph only sketches a family of hybrid methods; it gives no front representation, smooth-region update, jump solver, time step, invariant, or correctness statement from which a checkable algorithm could be formalized.

rows.source_label: Shock waves can only appear from nonlinear phenomena in the surrounding discussion of initially smooth small-amplitude waves

disposition.reason: The physical slogan leaves formation versus prescribed discontinuity, the shock/admissibility class, coefficient regularity, initial/boundary data, solution concept, and time quantifiers unspecified. These affect truth conditions: linear Riemann data already permits jumps. Smoothness preservation for constant-coefficient evolution is only a specified subcase, not coverage of the unrestricted slogan.

rows.source_label: The finite-volume high-resolution methods discussed are typically at best second-order accurate

disposition.reason: The qualified assertion fixes no method/reconstruction/limiter/time-integrator class, error norm, local versus global or spatial versus temporal order, data regularity, mesh/time relation, quantification of typical, or non-improvability bound for at best. An O(h^2) upper bound or one selected scheme does not establish this unspecified method-class claim.

rows.source_label: Hyperbolic equations with variable coefficients may not be in conservation form
Wave-propagation methods use Riemann waves rather than interface fluxes, apply beyond conservation form, and connect to flux differencing on conservation laws

disposition.reason: The asserted framework correspondence fixes no fluctuation operators, numerical interface update, applicability conditions, or equality relating wave propagation to flux differencing. These missing operators and hypotheses prevent a checkable mathematical correspondence in this passage.
